title: Ohio's rural voters could decide the Senate race in competitive election
content: Ohio, a state that has voted reliably for Republicans in recent elections, is considered competitive this year. The article notes that Democrats must secure the support of rural voters, who have previously backed Republican candidates, if they hope to prevail in the race for Senate control.
summary: Ohio is described as a reliably red state that has become competitive this year. Democrats need to win over rural voters who have previously backed Republicans to prevail.

title: Pentagon AI weapons often fail to follow agency guidelines, report says
content: A congressional watchdog report published in October indicates that the Pentagon is developing weapons and projects with AI capabilities that do not always strictly follow the agency’s own guidelines for responsible AI.
summary: A congressional watchdog report published in October states that the Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities. Officials acknowledge that these projects do not always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for responsible AI.
author: NPR Politics

title: Trinity College Dublin scientists reveal how cancer evades chemotherapy
content: Scientists at Trinity College Dublin have reported a breakthrough in understanding how cancer cells evade chemotherapy. The research reveals that these cells can enter a "zombie-like state" known as premature senescence, which allows them to survive the cell-killing effects of treatment. This state can also trigger the immune system’s wound-healing properties.
summary: Researchers at Trinity College Dublin have discovered how cancer cells evade chemotherapy by entering a "zombie-like state" known as premature senescence. This state allows the cells to attract the wound-healing properties of the immune system.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Discrimination Linked to Poor Mental Health for LGBTQ+ College Students
content:
A new national study led by Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health, Boston University School of Public Health, and Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Institute reveals that LGBTQ+ college students facing discrimination are significantly more likely to suffer from depression, anxiety, and suicidal thoughts. The research also indicates that these students are more prone to avoiding necessary health care. The study’s findings emphasize the substantial impact of discrimination on student mental health during a critical developmental stage.

The results of this largest study of its kind have been published in the journal Behavioral Medicine. By highlighting these persistent disparities nationwide, the research underscores the urgent need to address the specific challenges faced by LGBTQ+ students in higher education settings.
summary: A new national study found that LGBTQ+ college students experiencing discrimination are significantly more likely to suffer from depression, anxiety, and suicidal thoughts. The research, published in Behavioral Medicine, also indicates that these students are more likely to avoid needed health care.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Japanese study links fish consumption to reduced hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
content: A new prospective study from Japan has investigated the potential link between fish consumption and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, such as gestational hypertension and preeclampsia. The research analyzed data from Japanese women, specifically examining fish intake and the consumption of n-3 and n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids across various stages of pregnancy. The study's findings indicate a pattern that could have implications for preconception and prenatal nutrition strategies.
summary: A new prospective study from Japan examined whether fish intake before and during pregnancy is linked to hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. The research analyzed data on fish consumption and n-3 and n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid intake across different stages of pregnancy.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Invikafusp alfa stalls treatment-resistant cancers in first human trial
content: Early results from the first clinical trial of invikafusp alfa (invika) suggest the precision T-cell therapy may manage treatment-resistant cancers. The data indicates the drug can address malignancies that have resisted standard treatments, including conventional immunotherapy.
summary: Early results from the first clinical trial of invikafusp alfa indicate the treatment may manage cancers that have resisted other interventions. The therapy includes standard immunotherapy among the treatments it may help overcome.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study identifies new treatment targets for common bowel cancer in Ireland
content:
A study published today identifies potential new treatment targets for the most common type of colorectal cancer in Ireland. The research was conducted by an international team led by RCSI University of Medicine and Health Sciences and The Institute of Cancer Research, London.

The findings provide a roadmap for repurposing existing drugs and developing new ones. This approach aims to create more effective, personalized treatments for thousands of patients who currently have limited options.
summary: Study identifies new treatment targets for common bowel cancer in Ireland.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Scientists uncover molecular pillars shaping cell mitochondria
content:
Scientists have identified the molecular structures responsible for shaping mitochondria, the cellular organelles that supply most of the body’s energy. These powerpacks rely on a unique architecture consisting of two membranes, one nested inside the other, with a narrow gap between them known as the intermembrane space (IMS).

The organization of this tiny intermembrane space is critical to mitochondrial function, as it sustains the specific chemistry required for energy production.
summary: Mitochondria generate cellular energy using a distinctive architecture of two membranes separated by a narrow intermembrane space. The organization of this tiny space is critical to sustaining the chemistry of energy production.
author: Phys.org

title: Stellar collision may explain younger‑appearing planet‑forming disks in Orion Nebula
content: The Orion Nebula is a large star‑forming region visible to the naked eye. It contains young stars surrounded by gas and dust disks where planets form. Radiation from the massive central star, 1 Ori C1 (Theta‑1 Orionis C1), strips material from the disks, giving them tadpole‑like shapes. The title proposes that a stellar collision may explain why these disks appear younger than their stars.
summary: The Orion Nebula is a visible star‑forming region whose young stars are surrounded by gas‑and‑dust disks where planets form. Radiation from the massive central star 1 Ori C1 (Theta‑1 Orionis C1) strips material from these disks, giving them tadpole shapes, and a stellar collision may explain why the disks appear younger than their stars.
author: Phys.org

title: Mylar identified as promising insulator for lunar habitats
content:
Everyday Mylar has been identified as a promising insulator for lunar habitats. The material’s properties could help manage the extreme temperature swings encountered on the Moon.

Establishing a long‑term lunar presence requires addressing challenges that are easy to overlook on Earth. Lunar temperatures can range from hundreds of degrees below zero to boiling, making effective insulation essential for habitats.
summary: Everyday Mylar has been turned into a promising insulator for lunar habitats. Lunar temperatures can vary from hundreds of degrees below zero to boiling, requiring effective insulation for habitats.
author: Phys.org

title: NASA Tests RS-25 Engine No. 10001 at Stennis Space Center
content:
NASA teams at the Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, conducted a hot fire test of RS-25 engine No. 10001 on October 21, 2026. The test, documented by NASA photographer Danny Nowlin, lasted approximately 500 seconds, matching the duration of RS-25 engine firing during the launch of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket. The engine operated at a 111% power level during the trial.

Each Artemis mission utilizes four RS-25 engines to generate up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust for the SLS rocket. All RS-25 engines are verified for flightworthiness at NASA Stennis before operational use. Although this specific developmental engine will not be deployed in a flight, the test enabled NASA and its prime contractor, L3Harris Technologies, to collect critical data aimed at enhancing engine performance and reliability.
summary: NASA/Danny Nowlin Teams at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi tested RS-25 engine No.
author: NASA News

title: Storm Austen causes power cuts and travel disruption; second storm hits Scotland
content: Storm Austen has caused power cuts and travel disruptions across the UK. Millions of people remain under yellow weather warnings for wind and rain, as a second storm is forecast to hit Scotland and parts of northern England on Saturday.
summary: Millions of people remain under yellow weather warnings for wind and rain while Storm Austen causes power cuts and travel disruption. A second storm is expected to hit Scotland and parts of northern England on Saturday.

title: Impossible Machines: Declarative Programming for the Physical World
content: Hey all — Sharing a thought experiment I put together. The premise: what might declarative programming feel like for the physical world? We’re already familiar with this paradigm in software land (eg SQL etc where we declare what we want and the execution engine figures out how). I didn’t have access to an actuator so I mocked up the concept in software. The way it works is you demonstrate the effect and the system figures out how to achieve it. So say you want to ring a bell and you have a crank. The system will find a way to connect the two. If you add obstacles it figures out how to work around them (runs a constraint solver runs behind the scenes). I think what’s interesting about this is being able to think about the problem at a higher level of abstraction, with the system figuring out a way to achieve the intended effect. Anyways, curious to read reactions, feedback, and interesting ideas on how to extend this! Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50202746 Points: 36 # Comments: 7
summary: The developer presents a software simulation of declarative programming for the physical world, where users demonstrate a desired effect and the system determines how to achieve it. A constraint solver runs behind the scenes to find ways to connect actuators to effects while working around obstacles.
author: Hacker News

title: Developer seeks help finding Drop7 strategy to exceed 1 million points
content:
A developer has posted a project on Hacker News investigating optimal strategies for the puzzle game Drop7. The creator originally wrote a Java program for the game sixteen years ago and recently renewed their investigation to determine if an autonomous strategy can average more than one million points per game. While experienced human players can achieve this score through long-term strategic thinking, the best automated strategies currently developed average between 300,000 and 400,000 points.

The project is described as an experiment in using agents as research collaborators and evidence collectors. The developer has provided a global leaderboard where users can compete and submit human strategies, along with a GitHub repository for the project. The post seeks feedback from individuals with expertise in game theory, stochastic planning, learned value functions, or heavy-tailed evaluation regarding approaches to long-horizon action ranking. The submission has received nine points and has no comments.
summary: A developer is investigating whether an autonomous strategy can average more than one million points in the puzzle game Drop7. Current automated strategies average 300,000 to 400,000 points, while experienced human players can reach one million.
author: Hacker News

title: Vergecast debates if iPhone Duo should have been an iPad
content:
The Vergecast hosts David and Nilay discuss the recent review of the iPhone Duo, which received a score of 7 out of 10. The hosts acknowledge that this rating was not their initial plan and may change over time, citing the difficulty of evaluating a major new concept for the most popular smartphone in history. They debate whether the device deserved its current score and analyze how its perception might evolve.

During the episode, the hosts consider alternative product categorizations for the device. They reference John Gruber of Daring Fireball, who suggested the outer screen is the worst iPhone ever made. The discussion also explores whether the product would be viewed more favorably if it had launched as an iPad rather than an iPhone, or if it were simply named the iPad Duo.
summary: Vergecast hosts David and Nilay discuss whether the iPhone Duo deserved its 7/10 review score. They debate if the device would be better received if it were marketed as an iPad rather than an iPhone.
author: The Verge

title: SpaceX's Starshield throttled, disabling Ukrainian interceptors and causing casualties
content:
Starshield, the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink used by Ukraine, was recently throttled to block terminals traveling above certain speeds. This restriction caused Ukrainian interceptors designed to counter Russian drones to stop functioning at high speeds, facilitating attacks on the country’s energy infrastructure. The disruption reportedly resulted in two deaths and at least 17 injuries. The Ukrainian military stated it received no advance warning of the speed limit.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy characterized the action as a direct message from the US amid rising tensions.
summary: Starshield, the version of SpaceX's Starlink used by the Ukrainian military, was throttled to block terminals traveling above certain speeds. The speed restriction stopped Ukrainian interceptors from working at high speeds, facilitating Russian attacks that resulted in two deaths and at least 17 injuries, and the Ukrainian military said it received no advance warning.
author: The Verge

title: Soundcore Space 2 headphones drop to $106.49 on sale
content:
Soundcore’s newest Space 2 headphones are now available at an all‑time low price of $106.49, a $23 discount from the original $129.99 retail price. The sale is running on Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, making the upgraded model more accessible for buyers looking for budget‑friendly noise‑cancelling options.

The Space 2 is offered in three colors, including an attractive seafoam green. Customers can choose from the same three color options that were available for the earlier Space One model, ensuring a familiar aesthetic while enjoying the newer hardware.

Key improvements over the Space One include stronger active noise cancellation, especially for low‑frequency sounds such as trains and airplane engines. The headphones also deliver more accurate sound performance thanks to design upgrades, while retaining features that made the original popular, such as support for high‑resolution LDAC audio and the HearID 3.0 personalization tool that lets users adjust the sound profile after listening to sample tracks.

Battery life has been extended to 50 hours with ANC enabled and 70 hours without ANC, up from 40 and 55 hours on the original. The Space 2 also includes a 3.5 mm jack for wired listening when the battery runs low, and it automatically pauses playback when removed, helping users keep their place in songs or podcasts.
summary: Soundcore Space 2 headphones drop to $106.49 on sale.
author: The Verge

title: Abandoned Popcorn Time apps disabled to prevent bot army
content:
Researchers at Eye Security discovered that the updater for a Popcorn Time fork named "Time4Popcorn" remains active on numerous Windows, macOS, and Android devices worldwide. The software continues to contact abandoned web domains via unencrypted HTTP and utilizes an outdated, insecure version of Chrome.

The original Popcorn Time application, a torrent-streaming front end, has been abandoned for years despite remaining installed on millions of devices. These dormant installations pose a security risk by potentially forming a bot army, a threat that required the apps to be disabled to prevent exploitation.
summary: Researchers at Eye Security discovered that the updater for the abandoned Popcorn Time fork Time4Popcorn was still active on millions of devices. They disabled the updater to stop the software from phoning home over unencrypted HTTP and joining a bot army.
author: The Verge

title: Valve developer Mike Morasky mentions HLX code name at GameSoundCon
content: Gamers still hoping against hope for a true follow-up to Half-Life 2 (after so, so many years ) may remember last year's flurry of speculation that Half-Life 3 was finally nearing completion. Amid all those rumors, though, we never got any official sign from anyone inside Valve that a Half-Life project was currently in development. That changed this week thanks to an apparent slip-up during a panel at GameSoundCon, an industry conference devoted to "the art, technology, and business of game audio." In a panel devoted to Valve's use of open audio engines (captured in this Vimeo clip ), Valve composer and audio artist Mike Morasky let an interesting string of three letters slip while talking about the way the company implements high dynamic range (HDR) audio: Our HDR system is basically that's one of the three pieces that come together to make an HDR that you can easily optimize. And in fact, I think Deadlock has their own version of HDR. HLX has its own version, so on and so forth [emphasis added]. "HLX," of course, has been widely reported as the internal code name for Valve's next Half-Life project. The codename has shown up in Valve engine code since at least 2024, but it has never been referenced in public by a Valve employee until now (though Morasky was responsible for a close call in an interview last year). Read full article Comments
summary: Valve composer Mike Morasky referenced the internal code name HLX while discussing HDR audio during a panel at GameSoundCon. This marks the first time a Valve employee has mentioned the codename associated with the next Half-Life project in a public setting.
author: Ars Technica

title: Knicks sent employees fake offer of championship rings in phishing test: Report
content:
The New York Knicks organization conducted a phishing test by sending employees an email promising free championship rings, according to a report by The New York Times. The message, which was sent in late September, stated, “Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here,” and instructed staff to click a link to select from two ring designs.

The report noted that Madison Square Garden employees who clicked the link were required to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class. This action was taken to address the growing cybersecurity concerns of James Dolan, who is identified as the owner of the Knicks, the New York Rangers, and Madison Square Garden.

Such phishing tests are common in corporate environments to identify employees who may overlook signs of scams. These test emails typically appear to originate from the company but contain telltale indicators of phishing, such as misspelled domains in the sender’s email address.
summary: Knicks sent employees fake offer of championship rings in phishing test: Report.
author: Ars Technica

title: NIH board chair warns RFK Jr.'s vaccine clinic could damage hospital reputation
content:
At a recent meeting of the board that oversees the National Institutes of Health’s Clinical Center Research Hospital, chair Jack Leslie opened with introductions before shifting the discussion to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy. Leslie spent six minutes warning that Kennedy’s anti‑vaccine activities could tarnish the hospital, known as the “house of hope” for patients with rare conditions.  

Leslie criticized a stunt Kennedy staged at the hospital: a surprise ribbon‑cutting ceremony for his vaccine injury clinic. The ceremony featured a panel of individuals claiming to have been injured by vaccines, who sat behind placards reading “vaccine injured” and spoke with Kennedy and other high‑ranking Trump administration officials.  

Leslie said some might prefer he remain silent, but he believes silence would be a failing for the advisory board. He added that he has no concerns about studying potential vaccine injuries, noting that serious reactions are rare but real and that people who believe they have been injured should be taken seriously.
summary: Jack Leslie, chair of the NIH Clinical Center board, stated that Robert F. Kennedy's surprise appearance at a vaccine injury clinic opening could tarnish the hospital. Leslie warned that the event, which featured individuals claiming vaccine injuries, risks damaging the institution's reputation despite his support for studying rare reactions.
author: Ars Technica

title: Intel gets FCC waiver to use foreign-made robots in US fabs
content:
Intel secured a temporary exemption from a U.S. government ban that had raised concerns about the use of foreign‑made robots in its chip‑making facilities. The company requested a waiver to ensure it could continue deploying certain robotic vehicles in its U.S. semiconductor fabs. The Federal Communications Commission, which had issued the ban on specific foreign‑made robots, granted Intel’s request in an order published on October 22. The exemption allows Intel to use the robots for a period of one year.

The robots in question are automated guided vehicles that operate on tracks or predefined paths and typically require operator oversight. According to Intel’s website, these vehicles move materials and items around warehouses and factory floors. The FCC’s decision clarifies that Intel may maintain these robotic systems in its U.S. manufacturing plants despite the broader regulatory restrictions.
summary: Intel requested and received a one-year waiver from the FCC to continue using foreign-made automated guided vehicles in its US semiconductor manufacturing facilities. The agency granted the waiver on October 22 after Intel sought clarification due to uncertainty surrounding a ban on certain foreign-made robots.
author: Ars Technica

title: Crows Evaluate Visual Information Twice as Fast as Mammals
content:
Neurobiologist Andreas Nieder of the University of Tübingen highlighted a significant gap in understanding how avian brains process visual information, noting that birds lack the neocortex found in mammals. While research on monkeys using random-dot-motion tasks has established that primate neocortex neurons accumulate visual evidence over time until a decision threshold is crossed, it remained unclear how differently organized avian brains encode similar decisions. Nieder described this mechanism as the central question in the field.

The provided text indicates that crows can evaluate visual information twice as fast as mammals, a finding that addresses how these birds make decisions despite their distinct brain structure. This discovery offers insight into the neural processes underlying decision-making in species without a neocortex, contrasting with the well-documented evidence-gathering mechanisms observed in primate studies.
summary: In a random‑dot‑motion task, primates gather visual evidence until a threshold is reached, prompting a decision. Researchers at the University of Tübingen found that crows evaluate visual information twice as fast as mammals, raising questions about how avian brains encode decisions without a neocortex.
author: Ars Technica

title: Daytona hits $1B valuation backed by FirstMark and top angel investors
content: Daytona, an agent‑cloud startup, has reached a $1 billion valuation with backing from FirstMark and a roster of high‑profile angels. title: UAE Diplomat Lana Nusseibeh Enters UN Secretary‑General Race
content:
UAE’s star diplomat Lana Nusseibeh has entered the race for the UN secretary‑general position, directly challenging front‑runner Rebeca Grynspan. The timing of this entry comes as the global organisation faces a decisive period for its future direction.  

With Nusseibeh in the contest, the UN chief race now has the potential to produce the first ever female secretary‑general.
summary: UAE’s star diplomat Lana Nusseibeh has entered the race for the UN secretary‑general position, challenging front‑runner Rebeca Grynspan. The race could now lead to the first ever female secretary‑general.

title: US Designates Helium a Critical Material as Europe Scrambles for Supply
content: The United States has declared helium a critical material. The decision follows a global supply squeeze caused by war in the Middle East and export curbs imposed by Russia and China. Helium is essential for chipmaking, and Europe is scrambling to secure its share of the limited supply.
summary: The US has declared helium a critical material. War in the Middle East and export curbs by Russia and China are squeezing global supplies, leaving Europe scrambling to secure its share.
author: Euronews

title: France Extends Curfew, Bans Protests in Marseille and Lyon
content:
France is preparing for another weekend of protests after violence erupted during last week’s mobilisations. Paris has extended a partial curfew in parts of the city until Monday, while protests are banned altogether in Marseille and Lyon.  

70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, and only union demonstrations will be authorised.
summary: France has extended a partial curfew in Paris until Monday and banned protests in Marseille and Lyon. The government will deploy 70,000 security personnel on Saturday and allow only union demonstrations.

content: Israeli settlers and soldiers have repeatedly destroyed olive trees grown by Palestinian farmers in the West Bank. A video depicting trees being ripped up circulated online, but the footage was generated by artificial intelligence, not an actual recording.
summary: Israeli settlers and soldiers have repeatedly destroyed olive trees grown by Palestinian farmers in the West Bank. A video that appeared online showing trees being ripped up was later identified as an AI‑generated fabrication.

content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday warned of an imminent large-scale military operation in the West Bank and vowed to displace some residents of Hebron after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers in an attack.
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned on Friday of an imminent large-scale military operation in the West Bank. He vowed to displace some residents of Hebron after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers in an attack.

title: Gaza recovery teams have retrieved 1,000 bodies, thousands remain buried
content: One year after the Gaza ceasefire, Civil Defense officials report that recovery teams have retrieved 1,000 bodies from the rubble. They estimate that another 8,000 to 10,000 remain buried, including roughly 3,000 in zones under Israeli army control. The effort to locate and exhume the remaining victims continues.
summary: One year after the Gaza ceasefire, Civil Defense officials say recovery efforts have so far retrieved 1,000 bodies from the rubble. They estimate another 8,000 to 10,000 bodies remain buried, including about 3,000 in areas controlled by the Israeli army.
author: France 24

title: Israel election: Arab parties could become kingmakers as Likud and Yashar lack majority
content: Israel heads to a legislative election—the first since Hamas’s October 7 attacks—where neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party nor former army chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party is expected to secure a Knesset majority. Analysts note that Israel’s Arab parties could therefore influence the final outcome.
summary: Israelis are voting in the first legislative election since Hamas's October 7 attacks. Neither Prime Minister Benjamin #Netanyahu's Likud party nor former army chief of staff Gadi #Eisenkot's Yashar party is expected to win a Knesset majority, leaving Israel's Arab parties in a position to influence the outcome.

content: The olive harvest officially began in the West Bank on October 15, 2026, and the title notes that Israeli settlers wearing keffiyehs are attacking West Bank olive groves. Content reports an uptick in violence toward Palestinians by both Israeli settlers and soldiers, and says settlers and soldiers are using social media to promote an aesthetic, Instagram‑friendly, nationalistic view of these harvests.
summary: Israeli settlers wearing keffiyehs are attacking olive groves in the West Bank after the olive harvest officially began on October 15, 2026. The attacks coincide with an uptick in violence toward Palestinians by settlers and soldiers, who are also using social media to promote an Instagram‑friendly, nationalistic view of the harvests.

title: Netanyahu weighs West Bank operation before elections, says it won’t help politically
content: As Israel approaches a consequential parliamentary election amid renewed violence in the occupied West Bank, Yedioth Ahronoth Senior Journalist Ben-Dror Yemini offers a critical assessment of Benjamin Netanyahu's political prospects, the limits of military escalation and the shifting relationship between national security and electoral legitimacy. Since October 7, 2023 "Netanyahu is not popular anymore," Yemini argues, identifying the Hamas-led attacks as a decisive turning point in the Israeli prime minister's public standing.
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu is considering a West Bank operation as Israel approaches a parliamentary election amid renewed violence in the occupied West Bank. Senior journalist Ben-Dror Yemini says Netanyahu’s popularity has declined since the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas‑led attacks and that a military escalation would not improve his political prospects.
author: France 24

title: French riots spark curfews as protests spread to Italy, Spain, Portugal and Belgium
content: It's been a week that’s seen mass protests hijacked by violent rioters across France. The looting of shops, trashing of public buildings, the burning of Lyon’s Tourist Information and the iconic Limoges City Hall. After the riots, came the curfews, and the contemplation, who did what and why weren’t they stopped. Seditious groups, ultra left anarchists and opportunist criminals said President Macron, with a qualified mea culpa: failures in anticipation and authorities dropped the ball in intelligence gathering. Macron is out of breath, exhausted and disorientated claimed the Presidential Frontrunner Marine Le Pen, the far right leader now polling in an even stronger position for the Presidency. Foreign leaders had a free for all too, President Trump wading in and Israel’s prime minister settled old scores ahead of elections there. But France wasn’t isolated in its protests and unrest, Milan was a mirror image, with demonstrations in Spain, Portugal, Belgium too, An Autumn of Discontent, and more protests to follow this weekend:
summary: Violent rioters looted shops, trashed public buildings and burned Lyon’s Tourist Information and Limoges City Hall during a week of protests across France. Curfews followed and similar demonstrations were reported in Milan, Spain, Portugal and Belgium, with Marine Le Pen said to be polling stronger for the presidency.

title: Russia's attacks on Kyiv intensify, making 2026 one of war's bloodiest years
content: Russia’s attacks on Kyiv are becoming harder and more frequent, with 2026 described as one of the bloodiest years of the long war for the Ukrainian capital. DW has spoken with residents to report on daily life amid the intensified bombardment.
summary: Russia's attacks on Kyiv are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the war's bloodiest years for the city. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.
author: DW World

title: Storm Austen leaves thousands without power in south‑west England
content:
Storm Austen, the first named storm of the year, struck south‑west England, prompting school closures and widespread power outages. A gust of 76 mph was recorded at St Mary’s airport on the Isles of Scilly on Friday morning, and just before 11 a.m. National Grid reported that more than 16,000 homes in the region were without electricity.

Dozens of schools in Cornwall were also affected. Meanwhile, Storm Boelo is moving toward Scotland, Northern Ireland and the north of England.
summary: Thousands of homes lost electricity and schools were closed as Storm Austen struck south‑west England. A 76 mph gust was recorded at St Mary’s airport on the Isles of Scilly and the National Grid said more than 16,000 homes were without power, while dozens of schools in Cornwall were also affected.
author: Guardian World

title: Reform UK readies appeal after expected negative standards verdict on £5m gift
content:
Reform UK is preparing for a negative report from the standards commissioner concerning leader Nigel Farage’s failure to declare a £5 million gift from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne. Party insiders say they anticipate the initial verdict will be against Farage and are readying an appeal if the findings are adverse.  

The party described itself as being on “tenterhooks” and multiple Reform insiders confirmed they expect to mount a “fightback” through the appeals process after the report is issued.
summary: Reform UK is bracing for a negative report from the standards commissioner over Nigel Farage’s failure to declare a £5 million gift from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne. Party insiders say they expect the initial verdict to find against Farage and are preparing to appeal any adverse findings.
author: Guardian World

title: Ofcom says UK children still face same level of harm on social media despite crackdown
content: Campaigners call lack of progress ‘staggering’, as Ofcom also admits little change in severity of harm to children encountering unsafe content Landmark online safety measures have failed to limit the proportion of children suffering harm from social media, the UK’s online regulator has admitted, in an assessment branded “staggering” by campaigners. The proportion of children being fed unsafe content that often left them frightened, confused and upset, was almost unchanged, according to an Ofcom review of the first nine months of supposedly strict requirements on social media platforms such as TikTok and Instagram.
summary: Ofcom admitted that landmark online safety measures have not reduced the proportion of UK children harmed by social media. Its review of the first nine months of strict requirements on platforms such as TikTok and Instagram found the share of children receiving unsafe content that left them frightened, confused or upset was almost unchanged.
author: Guardian World

title: Jury hears Tommy Robinson threatened Daily Mail journalists, called a bully
content: Prosecution says Robinson guilty of harassment of Daily Mail journalists because we do not live in a ‘vigilante world’ Tommy Robinson is guilty of harassing two journalists because we do not live in a “vigilante world”, jurors have been told, as the prosecution sought to use the far-right activist’s words against him. Robinson had posted a video in which he told Daily Mail journalists he would find them after they wrote about his alleged role influencing England’s 2024 riots. He told them he had obtained details of where they and their families lived and warned them to abide by “men’s rules”.
summary: Jury hears Tommy Robinson threatened Daily Mail journalists, called a bully.
author: Guardian World

title: Criminals recruit children to vandalise Greater Manchester HMOs, police say
content: Police in Manchester say criminals are recruiting vulnerable individuals, including children, to damage houses they suspect are HMOs that may house immigrants. In recent weeks, dozens of such properties have been targeted across Greater Manchester, primarily in Salford and also in Stockport and Tameside.
summary: Police in Manchester believe criminals are recruiting vulnerable people, including children, to damage houses suspected of being HMOs. Dozens of properties have been targeted in recent weeks across Greater Manchester, mostly in Salford and also in Stockport and Tameside, because they are thought to hold immigrants.
author: Guardian World

title: Spain opposition deepfake video of PM's wife sparks outrage ahead of election

title: Study finds stupendously large black holes are not a major component of dark matter
content:
A new study indicates that black holes with masses exceeding that of entire galaxies are not a primary component of dark matter. Dark matter is a hypothetical substance believed to constitute approximately five-sixths of all matter in the universe, providing the gravitational force necessary to keep galaxies from spinning apart. While much remains unknown about this unseen material, including whether it exists, researchers have long considered black holes as potential candidates due to their extreme mass and difficulty in detection. The study specifically examined "stupendously large black holes" with masses greater than 100 billion times that of the sun. Objects in this category, particularly those weighing between one million billion and 10 million billion solar masses, would be heavier than whole galaxies. Currently, the largest known black hole weighs about 36 billion suns, and astronomers have not detected any stupendously large black holes despite observing numerous galaxies.

Christopher Gerlach, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics in Germany, noted that dark matter is typically conceptualized as a fine dust distributed throughout the cosmos. However, if dark matter were concentrated in a few gigantic objects like stupendously large black holes, the universe would appear grainy on very large scales. To test this hypothesis, the research team analyzed light from the early universe. Yann Gouttenoire, also of the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics, explained that for the first 380,000 years after the Big Bang, the cosmos was filled with hot plasma that trapped light. As the universe expanded and cooled, the plasma dissipated to form atoms, allowing light to travel freely. This light, known as the cosmic microwave background, serves as a snapshot of the infant universe covering the entire sky.

Antonio Iovino, a theoretical physicist at New York University, Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, stated that the temperature of the cosmic microwave background varies by about one part in 100,000 from place to place. This pattern reveals how matter was distributed in the early universe. The analysis showed that the cosmic microwave background is not grainy in the manner that stupendously large black holes would have produced. Consequently, Nicholas Leister, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics, concluded that these massive black holes cannot constitute a significant portion of dark matter.

The researchers clarified that their findings do not rule out the existence of stupendously large black holes, only that they do not make up a major fraction of dark matter. They suggested that another potential candidate for dark matter is relatively tiny black holes the size of asteroids. The team is currently investigating whether such small black holes can be ruled out as a major constituent of the mysterious substance. The study detailing these findings is scheduled for publication on Oct. 26 in the journal Physical Review Letters.
summary: Researchers analyzed the cosmic microwave background to determine that black holes more massive than entire galaxies cannot constitute a significant portion of dark matter. The study indicates that such objects would have made the early universe appear grainy, a pattern not observed in the light from the dawn of the cosmos.

title: Griffin-1 lunar lander passes critical tests at NASA JPL
content:
Voyager Technologies’ Griffin-1 lunar lander has successfully completed a series of critical environmental tests at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California. The spacecraft underwent rigorous simulations designed to replicate the extreme conditions it will encounter during its journey to the moon, including intense temperatures, shaking, and acoustic noise from launch through landing. According to JPL, the lander passed these tests with flying colors. An image captured on August 31 shows the vehicle inside JPL’s 25-foot-wide space simulator, highlighting the facility’s role in preparing robotic explorers for mission-critical challenges.

Charles Whetsel, manager for the Exploration Systems Development Office at JPL, noted that the Environmental Test Laboratory has supported robotic missions since the Ranger program in the mid-1960s. He expressed pride in providing expertise and facilities to support the new phase of commercial lunar exploration. The Griffin-1 mission is scheduled to launch later this year as part of NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative.

Upon reaching the moon, the robotic lander is expected to deliver over 1,100 pounds (455 kilograms) of cargo to a landing site near the lunar south pole. This payload includes science experiments and new technologies intended for surface testing. Among the cargo is Astrolab’s FLIP rover, which features a supercomputer designed to facilitate exploration of the lunar surface.

Beyond immediate scientific goals, the Griffin-1 mission aims to contribute to broader lunar development efforts. The data and experience gained from this robotic exploration will help prepare for the construction of a future crewed moon base. NASA plans to establish this base near the south pole within the next half-decade.
summary: Voyager Technologies' Griffin-1 lunar lander passed environmental tests at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory ahead of its scheduled launch later this year. The spacecraft will carry over 1,100 pounds of cargo, including Astrolab's FLIP rover, to the lunar south pole as part of NASA's CLPS initiative.

title: Taika Waititi’s Star Wars film joins unreleased Lucasfilm projects
content:
Taika Waititi has joined a long list of filmmakers who were expected to bring a new direction to the Star Wars franchise, only to find the studio appeared to get cold feet.  

The cost of producing a Star Wars film has risen sharply.  George Lucas’s 1977 original cost $11 million to make—about $60 million in today’s dollars—and has since earned $775 million at the global box office, including rereleases.  By contrast, the most recent entry in the saga, The Mandalorian and Grogu, reportedly cost $165 million and earned $346 million worldwide.  

Since 2019’s The Rise of Skywalker, only one Star Wars film—The Mandalorian and Grogu—has actually appeared in cinemas.  Yet Disney‑owned Lucasfilm has announced a small armada of other projects, often through press releases or at high‑profile celebrations, conferences and corporate jamborees, none of which has yet reached multiplexes.  The studio’s reluctance to produce new Star Wars movies has become a recurring theme in recent years.
summary: Taika Waititi has joined a long list of filmmakers whose Star Wars projects have not reached cinemas. Since 2019 only the film The Mandalorian and Grogu has been released, while other announced Star Wars projects remain unreleased.

title: Netflix cuts 1,000 jobs and replaces top film execs amid leadership shakeup
content:
Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters told investors this week that the company has nothing to be concerned about, despite recent organizational changes. The streamer announced it will lay off 1,000 employees across its product, tech, and legal departments. Additionally, the company is removing its chief content officer, film chairman, and film vice president.

Sarandos stated that Netflix has hired a new Chief Operating Officer, describing the individual as "one of the most effective at-scale operators in the entertainment industry," to help turn the company’s situation around. The article notes that while executive shake-ups are not uncommon, the frequency of these changes sends a concerning message.
summary: Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters announced the layoff of 1,000 employees and the removal of the chief content officer, film chairman, and film vice president. The company stated it hired a new COO to improve operations while assuring investors that the changes are necessary for the business.
author: The Verge

title: Apple Music features hidden first-generation iPod on 404 pages
content:
Users discovered a hidden, fully functional virtual iPod on Apple Music’s 404 error page on Friday. This easter egg, identified via social media, appears when accessing non-existent pages on the platform by adding random characters to the main URL. The virtual device features a recreation of the first-generation iPod.

The embedded player is stocked with tracks from the early 2000s, including Coldplay’s "Viva La Vida" and Gorillaz’s "Feel Good Inc." This nostalgic addition allows users to listen to music through the interface of the original portable media player.
summary: Apple Music now displays a virtual recreation of the first-generation iPod on its 404 error page. The hidden feature is stocked with music from the early 2000s and can be accessed by entering a non-existent URL.
author: The Verge

content: It’s been a long time since we had to rethink how to use an iPhone. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge The Duo is an entirely new kind of iPhone, so it comes with a bit of a learning curve. That's a wild thing to imagine, since the iPhone has had very few fundamental changes since its inception. But the Duo is built different. If you won the preorder lottery and managed to get your hands on one today, you'll see what that means. You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll lose track of the volume buttons as you turn the thing around. We've learned a few tricks over the past week of flipping and folding the Duo as much as we could. Here are our favorite tips and hacks for newly minted Duo owners. You can set orientation lock on each screen independent …
