title: Paris shopkeepers fear looting ahead of Saturday protest
content: Paris shopkeepers anticipate further losses ahead of a demonstration scheduled for next Saturday. Following vandalism observed during protests last weekend, some merchants are weighing the option of closing their stores, while others intend to remain open during the upcoming event.
summary: In Paris, shopkeepers fear further losses ahead of a demonstration planned for next Saturday. After last weekend’s protests saw scenes of vandalism, some are considering closing their shops, while others plan to stay open.
author: France 24

title: Three‑day US‑Israeli attack on Iran unlikely to radically change conflict
content:
Ahead of upcoming U.S. and Israeli elections, a 3‑day joint attack on Iran has been argued would not radically change the conflict. In a recent discussion, Jean‑Emile Jammine welcomed Federico Donelli, an associate professor of International Relations at the University of Trieste, to speak on the issue.

Donelli challenged the assumption that a short, intensive offensive would produce a decisive political outcome. He said the real question is whether military pressure is intended to constrain Iran’s capacity or to push Iran to the negotiating table, and whether such pressure can be translated into a sustainable political outcome without provoking a wider regional crisis. He also reminded that Iran still retains leverage over the United States.
summary: Ahead of US and Israeli elections, a three‑day joint attack on Iran is said to be unlikely to radically change the conflict. Associate Professor Federico Donelli of the University of Trieste said short intensive strikes may not produce a decisive political outcome and noted that Iran still has leverage over the United States.
author: France 24

title: Zelensky says Russia's latest attacks show no change in war attitude
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Thursday that Russia’s latest deadly attacks on Ukraine demonstrate “no real change” in Moscow’s attitude toward the war. The strikes occurred just hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin told U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff that Russia was ready to resume trilateral talks with Washington and Kyiv.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia's latest attacks on Ukraine show there has been no real change in Moscow's attitude toward the war. The deadly strikes came hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin told US envoy Steve Witkoff his country was ready to resume trilateral talks with Washington and Kyiv.

title: South Korean researchers propose new date for van Gogh's "Starry Night" sky
content: A team of South Korean researchers has put forward a new date for the night sky depicted in Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh's famed masterpiece "The Starry Night". Art historians have long assumed the stars were a product of the artist's fantasy or dated the scene to June 1889 based on the artist's location and other details, but astronomical details like the sliver crescent moon don't line up.
summary: A team of South Korean researchers has suggested a new date for the night sky depicted in Vincent van Gogh's painting "The Starry Night". They say the previously assumed June 1889 date does not align with astronomical details such as the sliver crescent moon.

content: Russian forces continue to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, yet thousands of residents remain or find it hard to evacuate. Many cite poverty, family ties and concern for beloved pets as reasons that make leaving the front‑line area painfully difficult.
summary: Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine. Thousands of residents either refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out, saying poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation difficult.

content: Europe and Vietnam are deepening economic and diplomatic ties. This closer cooperation has prompted concerns that Brussels may not be doing enough to address Hanoi’s human‑rights record, labor standards and trade imbalances.

title: Russia bombards Kyiv with missiles hours after agreeing to resume talks with Ukraine
content:
Russia launched a massive “demonstrative” attack on Kyiv, firing ballistic missiles overnight just hours after President Vladimir Putin said he had agreed to resume trilateral negotiations following talks with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff.  

The strike killed at least two people and wounded 22, including four children. Targets hit in the Ukrainian capital included the southern bridge over the Dnipro River, civilian houses, energy infrastructure, an ambulance station, office buildings and a clinic. Experts said the assault appears aimed at destroying energy infrastructure before winter and that U.S. “appeasement and flattery” will not achieve peace.
summary: Russia bombards Kyiv with missiles hours after agreeing to resume talks with Ukraine.

title: Macron bans “illegitimate” protests, permits recognized group demos with route changes
content:
French President Emmanuel Macron announced that “illegitimate” demonstrations would be banned over the coming days as France attempts to curb civil unrest. The decision follows a surge of street violence on the fringes of cost‑of‑living protests that some of the country’s worst in years. Macron made the statement after a meeting with intelligence officials and senior ministers.

He clarified that demonstrations organized by recognized groups would still be permitted, though their routes could be altered. Macron also said he would decide on concrete “next steps” for upcoming nationwide demonstrations.
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said demonstrations deemed “illegitimate” will be banned in the coming days as France seeks to curb civil unrest. He added that protests organized by recognized groups may proceed but their routes could be altered, and he will decide on concrete next steps for upcoming nationwide demonstrations.
author: Guardian World

title: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says mid-year budget will show weaker growth and higher unemployment
content:
Treasury is revising all the figures for the mid‑year budget update after Treasurer Jim Chalmers announced that December’s update will forecast weaker growth and higher unemployment. Economists have warned that the Australian economy faces a difficult six‑month outlook.

Chalmers is set to deliver a speech on Friday morning, two days after a senior Reserve Bank official suggested another interest‑rate rise could occur within two weeks. In that speech he will say higher inflation is putting people under pressure, tighter monetary policy is weighing on domestic activity, and the labour market is softening.
summary: Jim Chalmers said the December mid-year budget update will project weaker growth and higher unemployment for Australia. He warned that higher inflation and tighter monetary policy are pressuring households and softening the labour market, as economists anticipate a difficult six months ahead.
author: Guardian World

title: UN advisers warn 96% of shallow coral reefs could collapse by 2075
content:
An assessment by United Nations nature advisers indicates that nearly all shallow-water coral reefs globally, including Australia’s Great Barrier Reef, face a high risk of ecosystem collapse before 2075 due to global heating. The report highlights that approximately 24% of the planet’s reefs across more than 80 countries are already critically endangered. However, when the projected impacts of global heating are factored in, the percentage of reefs at risk rises to 96%.

Scientists involved in the assessment describe these findings as a “wake-up call” regarding the threat posed by climate change to marine ecosystems. The data underscores the severe vulnerability of coral reefs worldwide, with the vast majority expected to suffer significant degradation within the coming decades if current heating trends continue.
summary: United Nations nature advisers say almost all shallow‑water coral reefs, including the Great Barrier Reef, face a high risk of ecosystem collapse before 2075 because of global heating. The assessment reports 24% of reefs in over 80 countries are already critically endangered, rising to 96% when heating impacts are added.
author: Guardian World

content: John Lawrence Smart charged with being armed in a way that may cause fear but Perth lawyer expresses concern for mental health Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A man accused of making threats while armed with “improvised nunchucks” at a Western Australian MP’s electorate office could have been holding a musical instrument, not a weapon, a court has been told. title: Victorian MPs Georgie Purcell and Helen Haines cite safety fears after alleged constituent attack
content:
Hostility from constituents has long been reported as a feature of Victorian politics, affecting even premiers. The latest incident involves federal MP Helen Haines, who was allegedly attacked by a constituent in her regional Victorian electorate on Monday. The alleged assault prompted immediate concern among other female politicians.

Later that evening, Victorian upper‑house MP Georgie Purcell posted a statement on social media expressing support for Haines. Purcell said the alleged attack “sent chills down her spine” and noted that being a woman in politics has altered how she navigates everyday life, including where she parks her car, which routes she takes home and whether she holds public events at all. The remarks highlight a growing sense of insecurity among female Victorian MPs as they approach the upcoming election.
summary: Georgie Purcell, a Victorian upper house MP, posted on social media in support of Helen Haines after Haines was allegedly attacked by a constituent in her regional Victorian electorate. Purcell said the incident heightened safety concerns for women in politics, changing how she parks, travels and holds public events.
author: Guardian World

title: Bogong moth populations surge across eastern Australia
content: This animated map shows the insect’s population exploding in Australia’s eastern states, with the endangered species coming back from the brink If you live anywhere on the eastern side of Australia, you’ve probably noticed that bogong moths are back in a big way. While we don’t yet have figures from ecologist-led surveys to compare with previous years, there is a wealth of data on the great moth revival being generated by citizen scientists across the eastern states.
summary: An animated map shows the endangered bogong moth’s population exploding in Australia’s eastern states. Citizen scientists are generating extensive data on the species’ revival across the region.

title: Alberta seeks to restrict rights of migrant workers after earlier welcome
content: ‘Scapegoating non-permanent residents is not going to lower the cost of living,’ Vanesa Ortiz says When Vanesa Ortiz came to Calgary from Mexico, she found herself in a city gripped by winter. Outside the airport, it was -15C (5F). “I would come to understand that this was not an extreme cold,” she said. “But in the moment it was terrifying.

title: Sri Lanka win by two wickets after England's Harry Brook scores fastest 200 in ODIs
content: England captain Harry Brook scored 202 runs, the fastest 200 in One‑Day Internationals, during the match against Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka secured victory by two wickets, hitting a six with one ball left to win the game.

title: Angel Reese leads Atlanta Dream to 97-71 win, takes 2-1 lead in WNBA finals
content:
Angel Reese delivered a dominant performance for the Atlanta Dream, scoring 21 points and grabbing 12 rebounds in a 97‑71 victory over the Golden State Valkyries. The win on Wednesday night gave the Dream a 2‑1 lead in the WNBA Finals.  

Rhyne Howard added 16 points and Naz Hillmon contributed 15 points to the Dream’s tally. The team will host Game 4 on Saturday to try to close out the series.  

The Finals opener drew 17,099 fans to the arena and set a record with 2.1 million viewers on television.
summary: Angel Reese leads Atlanta Dream to 97-71 win, takes 2-1 lead in WNBA finals.

title: Edwards scores 45 as Timberwolves spoil Antetokounmpo's Heat debut
content:
Anthony Edwards scored 45 points, including nine three-pointers, as the Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the Miami Heat 131-106 in their season opener on Wednesday night. The victory spoiled the debut of Giannis Antetokounmpo with the Heat, who scored 35 points in his first game with the new team.

Edwards’ performance marked a historic milestone, making him only the third player in NBA history to record multiple 40-point games in season openers. He joins Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan in this distinction.
summary: Anthony Edwards scored 45 points to help the Minnesota Timberwolves defeat the Miami Heat 131-106 in the season opener. Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 35 points in his first game with the Heat.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Atlanta Dream host WNBA finals with 97-71 win over Golden State Valkyries
content:
The Atlanta Dream secured a 97-71 victory over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA finals, marking their first appearance in the championship series in 13 years. The match took place at State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta, where the Dream were described as being exactly where they wanted to be. The game featured a significant local celebrity presence, with Kerry Washington, Ludacris, and Cam Newton sitting courtside.

The event was transformed into a hometown spectacle by a crowd that filled the 20,000-seat venue. Fans wore matching sky-blue T-shirts and waved rally towels, creating an atmosphere so loud that the referee’s whistle was inaudible from the press section. The entertainment lineup included Quavo and TI headlining the halftime show, with two additional Atlanta rappers performing during other stoppages.

Following the final buzzer, DJ Khaled’s song “All I Do Is Win” played over the arena speakers as the Dream celebrated their win. The departing Golden State Valkyries were serenaded by the Atlanta crowd with the chant “ATL hoe!” Most fans remained until two minutes before the end of the game, after which they departed to beat traffic.
summary: The Atlanta Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 in Game 3 of the WNBA finals at State Farm Arena. The game featured a 20,000-seat crowd, celebrity appearances, and a halftime show by Quavo and TI.
author: Guardian Sport

title: San Francisco 49ers lead division despite offseason injuries and chaos
content:
San Francisco 49ers have emerged as early Super Bowl contenders, topping a tough division despite a challenging offseason. Head coach Kyle Shanahan’s participation in training camp was limited following a serious car crash, and team owner Jed York’s visit to an Ohio trailer park ended poorly. Additionally, multiple players suffered serious injuries.

The team maintains positive vibes with a strong defense led by safeties Malik Mustapha and Fred Warner, complemented by an impressive offense. However, the article notes that even these top teams possess flaws that opponents can potentially exploit.
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are currently top of their division despite a rough offseason marked by head coach Kyle Shanahan's limited camp participation and player injuries. Their strong performance is attributed to a defense led by Malik Mustapha and Fred Warner, along with an impressive offense.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Shola Ameobi recalls racism in Newcastle and role on executive team
content:
Shola Ameobi, the former Newcastle United striker and current member of the club’s executive team, has spoken about his experiences with racism during his childhood in Newcastle. Having moved from Nigeria at the age of six, Ameobi recalls facing harassment in the late 1980s and 1990s. He described instances where he feared for his safety, stating that he was chased by groups of people who targeted him because of his appearance.

Ameobi noted that these incidents were frequent, forcing him to sprint away from individuals who did not like him. He explained that the experience created a constant sense of worry about moving from one place to another, requiring him to be highly aware of his surroundings. According to Ameobi, the situation felt as though he had to hide parts of himself to pursue his passions, marking a difficult period in his life before he rose to prominence as a footballer and derby hero.
summary: Former striker Shola Ameobi describes experiencing racism and harassment while growing up in Newcastle after moving from Nigeria at age six. He reflects on his journey from being a derby hero to becoming a member of the executive team.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Harry Kane says Ballon d'Or wait is 'very stressful' for family
content:
Harry Kane has stated that the uncertainty surrounding his potential Ballon d’Or win is causing significant stress for his family, as they are subjected to constant questions about the outcome. The Bayern Munich and England striker, who is the odds-on favourite for the prestigious individual honour, admitted that while he tries not to think about the suspense, it is difficult to avoid. The award is scheduled to be revealed at the London Palladium on Monday night, a moment Kane accepts is part of the show.

Kane’s strong candidacy is supported by his prolific scoring record. The 33-year-old tallied 61 goals for Bayern Munich and 12 for England last season. In the current campaign, he has already scored 10 goals for Bayern and six for England. His recent performances include Wednesday night’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena, where he scored a penalty and provided a precise through ball that assisted Alphonso Davies in equalizing the match.
summary: Harry Kane admits the uncertainty of waiting for the Ballon d'Or announcement is very stressful for his family. The Bayern Munich and England striker is the odds-on favourite to win the award after a prolific run of form.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England v Sri Lanka: Duckett survives run-out chance in Rawalpindi ODI
content:
England and Sri Lanka commenced their men’s tri-series one-day international in Rawalpindi, with play beginning at 9am BST. In the third over, England scored five runs without losing a wicket, with Harry Banton on two and Phil Duckett on three. Duckett survived a run-out chance after taking a quick single on the off side, as Arachchige’s throw bounced past the stumps at the bowler’s end.

The over featured limited scoring, highlighted by a single big stroke from Banton that failed to beat the cover fielder. Sri Lanka bowled excellent length, while England appeared to be assessing the pitch conditions before attempting more aggressive shots.
summary: England are batting against Sri Lanka in a one-day international in Rawalpindi, with the score at 5-0. Phil Duckett survived a run-out opportunity after taking a quick single on the off side.

title: Strongmen like Trump would destroy the planet out of pure spite – and Brazil shows we’re all in peril | George Monbiot
content: If Flávio Bolsonaro is elected, Brazil’s ecosystems will face collapse. The ruling class would rather burn the world than share it with the poor However grim the trajectory might seem, I’ve always believed that sense will ultimately prevail. As the great perils of dismantling the living world become increasingly obvious, even the most rapacious exploiters must come round. Nobody wants to live on a dead planet, do they? There are – or were – signs that this wasn’t just wishful thinking. Since 2015, mostly thanks to China, the area of the planet being reforested has increased, while thanks in large part to Brazil, the global rate of forest destruction has declined. The area of the Brazilian Amazon forest cleared each year is one-sixth of what it was when records began in 1988. In the past four years, as a result of Brazilian government policy, the deforestation rate has fallen by 71%. If Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is re-elected president on Sunday, the country could reach zero deforestation by 2030. The arc of the moral universe seems to have bent towards justice.

title: WD report warns AI inference generates hidden storage costs up to 130x output size
content:
Executives often picture AI costs in terms of GPUs, power consumption and silicon shortages, but a recent WD analysis highlights that data‑storage expenses are a substantial, and frequently overlooked, component of AI infrastructure. The analysis notes that every inference request leaves behind data that must be retained, creating a continuous storage burden that grows as AI usage expands.

A concrete example comes from internal measurements of AI‑generated video. An 8‑second clip delivered to a user as a 3.97 MB 720p file generated more than 500 MB of backend data—including logs, cached context, immediate renders, backups and safety records—representing a 130‑fold increase over the user‑visible file size. When enterprises produce longer, higher‑resolution video, the backend footprint can reach hundreds of gigabytes per clip, and the overall storage demand is accelerating. McKinsey projects AI inference demand to grow at a 35 % compound annual growth rate through 2030, outpacing the 22 % growth projected for training and eventually accounting for over 40 % of total data‑center demand.

A WD‑sponsored IDC white paper that surveyed 763 IT and business decision‑makers found that nearly 95 % of respondents observed an increase in data volume due to generative AI in the past year, with roughly 61 % reporting growth of 25 % or more. The same survey indicated that 96 % anticipate a need for faster archive retrieval to support inference or retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG). A senior product manager at a hyperscale cloud service provider quoted in the report said that additional storage serves as an optimization to keep GPUs busy, noting that “hours of GPU idle time becomes very expensive, very fast.”

The analysis warns that storage spending can outpace compute budgets. While compute budgets tend to follow predictable cycles, storage costs may rise 25 % year over year, eventually eclipsing the line items that receive the most attention. Because data generated during inference—model logs, synthetic outputs and results—remains retained, it can become an input for future AI workloads, turning archives that were once rarely accessed into active assets.

To address these challenges, organizations are urged to adopt an architecture that balances performance with capacity across warm, cool and cold storage tiers. The report recommends treating archives as reusable resources for RAG and inference, establishing clear data‑retention policies, and aligning storage procurement with the full AI data lifecycle rather than solely with training‑time performance needs. It also proposes three questions for budgeting teams: what is the data‑retention policy for AI‑generated content; is storage procurement tied to training performance or data lifecycle; and would storage costs double if AI usage doubled. According to the analysis, many organizations cannot answer these questions confidently, indicating a gap that should be closed before the next budgeting cycle.
summary: Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs.

title: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort review – Wii Sports lives on in this effortlessly appealing collection of games
content: Nintendo Switch 2; Nintendo/Nintendo Bringing a holiday vibe and a generous selection of sport-themed games, this is exactly what you want from a family video game When the first Nintendo Switch Sports brought the effortless fun of Wii Sports back into my living room in 2022, I was frankly delighted. My small children discovered the pleasure of waving a controller around in enthusiastic imitation of a tennis player, and the surprising subtlety of virtual bowling, working out how to twist the wrist just right to guarantee a strike. I did not expect this game to become a family fixture for the next several years as my kids got older and climbed up the online ranks in all six of its sports (plus the two that were added as free updates). Switch Sports is so beloved in my household that the release of Switch Sports Resort this week is the most anticipated gaming event of the year. To be fair, my children are a bit young for Grand Theft Auto. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort brings three of the six sports back – tennis, bowling, and volleyball – alongside golf and basketball. Then there are seven entirely new sports: boxing, table tennis, archery, thumb wrestling, skateboarding, jetski, and piloting a little prop plane. They are all intuitive, easy to get the hang of on the first or second attempt – some have more legs than others, in the long run – and all of them, crucially, are a little bit silly. Thumb wrestling in particular is cheerfully absurd, giving your characters gigantic thumbs on hands the size of their heads.
summary: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort review – Wii Sports lives on in this effortlessly appealing collection of games.

content: Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (D-Ga.) warned on Wednesday that President Trump’s military operations against Iran could cost Republicans seats in the November elections. content: Saudi officials confirmed that an attack by Iranian-backed Houthis on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person and injured eight others on Wednesday evening. The General Authority of Civil Aviation stated that the rebel group targeted the airport in the eastern city.

title: King's AI model detects faulty DNA repair in ovarian cancer from tissue images
content:
Researchers at King’s have developed an AI model capable of detecting faulty DNA repair mechanisms in ovarian cancer cells by analyzing tissue images. The model can accurately identify tumors containing broken repair processes, which may allow clinicians to select treatments that exploit this specific flaw.

The findings, published in Nature Communications, suggest the technology could evolve into a low-cost and widely accessible diagnostic tool for the future.
summary: Researchers at King's developed an AI model that analyzes tissue images to detect broken DNA repair mechanisms in ovarian cancer cells. This tool could allow clinicians to select treatments that exploit the identified flaw.

title: Blocking cellular stress pathway may preserve insulin‑producing beta cells
content:
Researchers at Weill Cornell Medicine have identified a molecular pathway that contributes to the death of insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. Experiments using preclinical models and human pancreatic cells demonstrated that blocking specific proteins within this pathway helped protect beta cells from excessive cellular stress.

The findings, recently published in the Journal of Clinical Investigation, suggest a new strategy to preserve the cells responsible for regulating blood sugar. This approach may potentially offer a treatment option for type 2 diabetes.
summary: Researchers at Weill Cornell Medicine found that blocking proteins in a cellular stress pathway protects insulin‑producing beta cells from death. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Investigation, suggests a new strategy to preserve these cells and potentially treat type 2 diabetes.

title: Canada’s youngest children physically active, study reveals
content: Canada’s youngest generation is off to a good start for being physically active, but there is still room to grow. A first‑ever national assessment focused on children under age 5, led by a University of Alberta researcher, highlights both the progress and the opportunities for improvement.
